text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A Turkish delegation visiting Tehran proves that there are Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrilla camps in Iran.
- President Suleyman Demirel says the value of secularism should be appreciated.
- The number two in the Sudanese government is invited to Turkey to attend Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party congress on Oct 13.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz calls on parliament to take over the the reins of foreign policy from Erbakan's government.
- Security forces find a booklet on regulating the sex lives of militants written by PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan.
- Conservative coalition partner is angered by arguments on whether Erbakan's visit to Libya will be an official one.
- Turkey's hope in farming and breeding lies in big farms.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller fails to overcome U.S. mistrust of Turkey in her 10-day visit.
- Islamic law experts say executions by Taleban militia in Afghanistan are contradictory to Islam.
